interpretation: Four select attempts end with an empty control value and no captured keyboard, input or change events. The source uses WebElement.send_keys with an option-label initial and Tab. The helper did not meet its trusted-event or final-value requirements.

The two upload attempts select the expected metadata and record trusted input, change and Save-image click events. The application displays its pre-request construction/read failure message and the persisted projects remain version 1 without sources.

The upload catch covers source list mapping, fileBase64, and crypto.randomUUID. fileBase64 awaits File.arrayBuffer, converts bytes to a string in 8192-byte chunks, then calls btoa. The report does not record the caught exception or its exact stage.
The same-page setProject had already called crypto.randomUUID before upload. That source fact weakens, but does not experimentally disprove, a randomUUID capability hypothesis.
Three datetime interactions still reached exact requested values with trusted events. They are partial observations inside failed cases and add no product passes.
All six original native case outcomes remain failing. No CSV or XLSX native download was reached. The intake case that passed run 90 now fails at the revised select helper.
Run 91 adds passive page reads and event capture. Those observations change timing, so neither these failures nor a subsequent success establishes the original run 88/90 upload or review-save cause.
